vulnerability.name: GHSA-pmwq-pjrm-6p5r
vulnerability.description: in-toto-golang and in-toto-python use inconsistent negation operators in artifact rule glob patterns

statements.status_notes: Fixed upstream rather than triaged. docker/compose v5.6.0 resolves github.com/in-toto/in-toto-golang v0.11.0, the release that aligns the glob-negation operators in artifact rule patterns, and the source-built Compose plugin embeds that version, so the v0.10.0 build this statement used to cover is no longer shipped. The product below is the version the image carries now, and this statement records the resolution rather than suppressing a finding.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93687
vulnerability.description: braces is vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested glob patterns (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm)

statements.impact_statement: braces 3.0.3 can exhaust the stack while parsing a deeply nested glob pattern, so exploitation requires an adversary to control the pattern text that braces compiles. In Sencho, braces enters the production image through micromatch, which http-proxy-middleware uses to compile the proxy context and path-filter patterns once at startup from static configuration; request URLs are matched against the compiled matcher and are never compiled as patterns. The remaining occurrences are development-time watchers (chokidar under nodemon and the TypeScript watcher) watching fixed paths. No request-controlled input reaches the braces parser, so the vulnerable code cannot be triggered by a remote adversary. No patched release exists: 3.0.3 is the newest published version and the advisory lists no fixed version, so the dependency audit gate honors this statement instead of blocking every change.
